item.content:encoded: We have a window that we use, air quotes around the word window, that it uses a TV with a video feed of the outside of our habitat. And we can see the Martian sunrise with it out the window, and then the sun basically goes over our head and we eventually see the shadow of our habitat on the ground and eventually, throughout night we see the stars. And it's really pretty. If I could sum up Chapea in just a couple of words, the words would be, almost Mars.

item.title: A penny in a clear pool: how we see dark matter — clip from Encore: Welcome to the Dark Side (800.0-851.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】看不见的暗物质怎么被看见：想象晴天里一池清水，池底的硬币看起来变了形——光被水弯折了；远方星系的光被暗物质弯折，也是同一个道理。 【Reels 角度】看不见的东西怎么证明它存在？一枚池底的硬币告诉你：光被弯折的地方，就有暗物质。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NASA endorsement implied; full-episode music cues do not appear in this speech segment. 【来源】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-dark-side-encore/ 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-27 【发布时间精度】exact_encore（Inherits parent original publish date (Megaphone RSS Tue, 22 Sep 2026 13:03:00 -0000; episode originally published 2023); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-27 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:nasa.gov:curious-universe:roman-dark-side-encore 【父集链接】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-dark-side-encore/ 【片段】原集 800.0-851.5 秒，51.5 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/nasa-roman-dark-side-clip-penny.mp3
item.content:encoded: And I can use an analogy here. Imagine you're standing on a very calm day in front of a very crystal clear pool, and you throw a penny to the bottom of the pool. Now, you can't really see the water because it's crystal clear, but you can see the penny at the bottom of the pool and anyone who's done this knows that you see a distorted view of that penny. It doesn't appear as it would just on the ground. And that's because the light from the penny is traveling through the water and the light is bent by the water. So in this analogy, that penny is like the distant galaxy and the water is like the dark matter. So we don't actually see the dark matter. You don't actually see the water, but you know it's there. You know the water is there because you see a distorted view of the penny. And we know the dark matter is there because we see a distorted image of these background galaxies.

item.title: Ferdinand Hassler: the first superintendent of the Coast Survey — clip from Origins of NOAA's National Ocean Service (236.9-289.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NOAA Ocean Podcast 【主题】ocean-environment 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】首任局长 Hassler：学法律出身的瑞士移民，因测绘经验被杰斐逊看中，成了海岸测量局第一任局长。 【Reels 角度】学法律的人怎么成了美国第一个海洋测量局长？瑞士移民 Hassler 的故事。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NOAA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. item.content:encoded: That's right. So the first superintendent of the Coast Survey was a Swiss émigre named Ferdinand Hassler. And Hassler had studied law but then decided science was his passion. So he studied math. He had done a survey of one of the Cantons in Switzerland and had great experience. But he decided that he wanted to emigrate to the United States, and he felt that he had real skills to contribute to the development of the nation. And he was suggested to Thomas Jefferson. Jefferson, like many of the founding fathers, had a real scientific bent and saw a talented, experienced person who he could trust to establish this agency. He saw that in Hassler and appointed him.

item.title: Keeping an open mind: the most exciting science is the thing you didn't expect — clip from Roman Series: Why NASA’s Roman Space Telescope Will Make Unexpected Discoveries (377.6-427.6s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】保持开放心态：造出能力全新的天文台时，最激动人心的科学一定是你没预料到的东西；Roman 不挑一颗星系、一颗恒星，而是以极高灵敏度扫过整片天区——研究已知的，也找到那些你根本没想到要找的东西。 【Reels 角度】最激动人心的科学是你还没想到的：保持开放心态，跟着意外走——Roman 不是挑一颗星星看，而是把整片天区扫进来。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NASA endorsement implied; the episode's only music cue (Curiosity theme) does not appear in this speech segment. 【来源】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-deepdive-podcast/ 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-28 【发布时间精度】exact（Inherits parent original publish date (Megaphone RSS Thu, 27 Aug 2026 12:59:00 -0000); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-28 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:nasa.gov:curious-universe:roman-deepdive 【父集链接】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-deepdive-podcast/ 【片段】原集 377.6-427.6 秒，50.0 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/nasa-roman-deepdive-clip-openmind.mp3
item.content:encoded: So I'm keeping an open mind. I think when you build an observatory that has profoundly new capabilities, the most exciting science is going to be the thing that you didn't expect. So you want to approach what you're going to do with the observatory and how you're going to use it with something of an open mind so that we can pivot to following the surprises, following the things that are most impactful. With Roman, we're discovering space on steroids. Because we do large surveys, we're not picking a galaxy and going to study that galaxy. We're not picking a star to go and look at that star. We're mapping out large regions of the sky with extraordinary sensitivity. And we're going to find all the things that are there. So we're going to study the things that we know about and we're going to find the things we didn't even know to look for.

item.title: The largest clean room of its kind: eight stories tall, two basketball courts — clip from Roman Series: The Technology Inside NASA’s Newest Space Telescope (424.7-458.4s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】世界最大的无尘室：Roman 在戈达德航天中心 8 层楼高的无尘室里组装，面积可放两个篮球场，恒温 68 华氏度、湿度 45%；整面墙是 8 层楼高的滤网，能滤掉小至红细胞的微粒——因为一粒灰尘都可能毁掉一台太空望远镜。 【Reels 角度】世界上最大的无尘室长什么样：8 层楼高、两个篮球场大、恒温恒湿，整面墙的滤网能拦住红细胞那么小的微粒。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NASA endorsement implied; the episode's music cues (including the Rich Formula transition immediately before this speech segment) do not appear in this speech segment. 【来源】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-engineering/ 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-28 【发布时间精度】exact（Inherits parent original publish date (Megaphone RSS Tue, 25 Aug 2026 12:59:00 -0000); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-28 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:nasa.gov:curious-universe:roman-engineering 【父集链接】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-engineering/ 【片段】原集 424.7-458.4 秒，33.7 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/nasa-roman-engineering-clip-cleanroom.mp3
item.content:encoded: The clean room where Roman was built at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland is the largest clean room of its kind in the world. It's massive, eight stories tall, with enough floor space to fit two basketball courts. Inside this room, it is exactly 68 degrees Fahrenheit and exactly 45 percent humidity. There's a carefully calibrated air purifying system that is constantly circulating clean air. An entire wall of this room is an eight-story grid of air filters, which can filter out particles as small as a red blood cell.

item.title: Monitor as a testbed: new 3D imaging can spread to other wrecks — clip from USS Monitor 3D Mapping (559.7-604.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NOAA Ocean Podcast 【主题】ocean-environment 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】Monitor 当试验场：这套新成像技术不只拍 Monitor，还能用到更多沉船、沉没飞机甚至原住民遗址——关键是又快又准。 【Reels 角度】沉船变试验场：1862 年的 Monitor 试成功的新成像，能复制到别的沉船上吗？答案是能，而且很快。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NOAA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NOAA endorsement implied. 【来源】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/aug26/nop85-uss-monitor-3d-mapping.html 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-26 【发布时间精度】date_only（Inherits parent original publish date (NOAA page DC.date.created 2026-8-21, date only); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-26 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:oceanservice.noaa.gov:podcast:aug26:nop85-uss-monitor-3d-mapping 【父集链接】https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/aug26/nop85-uss-monitor-3d-mapping.html 【片段】原集 559.7-604.5 秒，44.8 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/noaa-uss-monitor-3d-85-clip-testbed.mp3
item.content:encoded: Do you suppose this new imaging technology will be used on more shipwrecks? Like saltwater and freshwater? Yeah, I hope by basically using Monitor as a testbed, and that's one of the wonderful things about Monitor, that where it's always been pushing technology innovation from 1862 to today, bringing all those new technologies to bear. That, you know, people would look at the example of what we achieved on Monitor with Northrop Grumman using this technology and how it can now be used and applied to other sites as well. You know, whether that be shipwrecks, maybe it's sunken aircraft. You know, maybe there's sunken indigenous sites. You know, just the technology and the resolution we can see for these things is mind-blowing. And the fact that we can collect that so quickly with the AUV, too, is very special.

item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】Roman 一旦升空，就会把广角相机对准银河系中心巡天：一次成像就能看到数十万颗恒星，用凌星法和微引力透镜法同时搜寻它们周围的行星；大多数恒星都有行星，所以这次普查预计将新增多达 10 万颗系外行星。 【Reels 角度】银河普查：Roman 将盯住银河系中心，一次成像看数十万颗恒星，预计新增 10 万颗系外行星——太阳系到底常不常见，答案就在这次普查里。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. item.content:encoded: Once Roman launches, the science team is going to turn the Wide Field Instrument towards the core of the Milky Way galaxy and scan for exoplanets. The wide field instrument is going to stare towards the center of our galaxy where it can see literally hundreds of thousands of stars in a single image at once. And it can use one of these two indirect detection methods, the transit method or the microlensing method, to search for planets around hundreds of thousands of stars at once. We know that most stars have planets. And so it's probably no surprise then that that with these surveys, the Wide Field Instrument will detect perhaps 100,000 planets.

item.title: Dark energy, explained with a thrown ball — clip from Roman Series: NASA’s New View of the Dark Universe (1363.9-1401.8s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】我们对暗能量几乎一无所知，只好先给它贴个标签：想象把球抛向空中，本以为它会落回手中——这就是人们原以为宇宙会做的事；结果却是宇宙越胀越快，球越飞越远、越来越快。这很反直觉，也出乎所有人意料。 【Reels 角度】暗能量先贴标签、再用抛球讲清：本以为抛出去会落回，结果越飞越快——反直觉，才是关键。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. Reusable with no NASA endorsement implied; none of the episode's music cues appears in this speech segment (between Pressurization Trailer and Tentative Surge cues in the official transcript). 【来源】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-series-nasas-new-view-of-the-dark-universe/ 【采集日（北京时间）】2026-10-29 【发布时间精度】exact（Inherits parent original publish date (Megaphone RSS Tue, 11 Aug 2026 13:08:00 -0000); clip itself was modelled 2026-10-29 Beijing, GUID does not use collection time.） 【父集 GUID】urn:podcast:nasa.gov:curious-universe:roman-dark-universe 【父集链接】https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/roman-series-nasas-new-view-of-the-dark-universe/ 【片段】原集 1363.9-1401.8 秒，37.9 秒，原声，未加 BGM，文件：clips/nasa-roman-dark-universe-clip-ball.mp3
item.content:encoded: We have basically no idea what's making that happen, but we had to put some kind of label on it, and that's dark energy. There's an analogy that you can kind of think of. If you imagine yourself holding a ball and you throw the ball up in the air and you know that it's going to come back and land in your hand. So this is originally what people thought was happening with the universe, that it would expand out and it would come back down again. But what we found was that the universe was expanding faster and faster. And so that's like if you throw a ball up in the air and then it shoots away from you faster and faster and faster. It's very counterintuitive. People weren't expecting this result.

item.title: One photon at a time: seeing exoplanet atmospheres — clip from Launching Soon: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope (159.0-206.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】在遥远恒星周围，科学家已发现数千颗系外行星；Roman 将看向银河系中心，一次成像就能看到数十万颗恒星，预计还会发现数千颗；更重要的是，它将用前沿技术看清行星细节——这些行星暗到来自它们的光子每几秒甚至每分钟才抵达相机一个，科学家只能从一个小光斑里推测大气成分。 【Reels 角度】从“已发现数千颗系外行星”到“一次看数十万颗恒星”，最后落到最动人的细节：来自一颗行星的光子，每几秒甚至每分钟才抵达相机一个。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. item.content:encoded: Far away from us, around distant stars, scientists have already found thousands of these exoplanets. Roman will look toward the center of our own Milky Way. Where it can see literally hundreds of thousands of stars in a single image at once. We know that most stars have planets. Which means Roman will detect thousands more exoplanets out there. With a cutting-edge piece of technology, Roman will see far more detail of some planets than we've ever seen before. These planets are so incredibly faint that you get one photon, one particle of light. Arriving at our camera from one of those planets once every few seconds or maybe even once every minute. So we are getting one little smudge to try to tease out what the atmosphere might be made of.

item.title: Can you say that again? A train-call assignment to Artemis III — clip from Meet the Artemis III Crew (330.7-376.5s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】Parmitano 在火车上接到电话，得知自己将担任 Artemis III 飞行员：话一时没听进脑子，追问“能再说一遍吗”，在公共场合不敢出声，最后在几天后首次与乘组见面时倍感荣幸。 【Reels 角度】火车上的一通电话：Parmitano 得知自己将担任 Artemis III 飞行员——话没听进脑子、追问“能再说一遍吗”、在公共场合不敢出声的狂喜。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. item.content:encoded: And so I answered the phone, and the boss told me, Hey, Luca, I want you to know that we want you to be the pilot on the Artemis III mission. And I was very much unprepared for that answer. And so it went through one ear, it didn't register in my brain, came out the other ear. And I literally said, Can you say that again? And it told me the same words. And then it did register, but I was in a public environment, so I knew that I couldn't say anything out loud. So I was literally speechless, which doesn't happen very often. And then I was very, very honored when I, when I met the crew for the first time a couple of days later.

item.title: Happy tears, relief tears — and ice cream at JPL — clip from Catching Up With Perseverance on Mars (240.4-278.9s)
item.description: 【节目】NASA's Curious Universe 【主题】science-space 【形态】audio, text 【生产形态】ready-clip 【摘要】Perseverance 着陆成功后，Katie 喜极而泣：如释重负的眼泪过后是“我们的工作才刚刚开始”；而 JPL 有个传统——用一箱冰淇淋慰劳火星时间的漫长夜班，疫情期间则改成送到她家门口。 【Reels 角度】着陆成功那一刻的眼泪：Katie 的如释重负与“我们的工作才刚刚开始”，接上 JPL 的冰淇淋传统——火星时间里的漫长夜班，也有人情味。 【许可证】Public domain：Excerpt of a US federal government work (NASA official podcast), generally not copyrighted 【权利说明】Clip is original speech only, no BGM added. item.content:encoded: I just burst into tears because just the swell of emotion, it was just too much. And I just cried. I cried happy tears, relief tears. And then I was like, Oh my gosh, our job is just starting. And of course, the engineers are celebrating a lot of them. You know, they're done. They move on to another project. They've gotten the rover to Mars. And for us, it was like, oh, no, now it gets down to business. And so it was like, Okay, we've got a long night ahead of us. There's a tradition at JPL to make working the long, hard hours of Mars time a little sweeter. Mission Control has a chest full of ice cream. So some of Katie's colleagues improvised the pandemic version. They had ice cream delivered to her front door.

item.content:encoded: break the grip of the rip, you see an image of a rip current, and it gives guidance to people on what to do if you're caught in a rip current, which is to stay calm, don't swim straight back to shore, don't fight the current, swim out of the current along the beach, you're out of the current and then back to the beach at an angle. And that guidance has largely been pretty successful. We did some surveys recently and found something like 90% of those surveyed, of those beach goers that we surveyed, were generally aware of rip currents and what to do if they're caught in one. But despite that success, as I mentioned, we're still seeing the same number of rip current drownings every year, something like 100 rip current drownings per year.
